exact_statement: For every even k>=4, r>=2k, and C>=6, let F be the canonical quadratic bent k-bit function and its zero-vertex point flip, activated by r fresh point controls and selected by a fair physical selector. On the complete selector-controls-adjacent-data-pairs tree with irrelevant inputs skipped and constant leaves, the minimal nonnegative reserve Q*_v=[D_v-C Inf_v+average Q*_children]_+ vanishes at every control node and even point-edited paired-data entry. Odd edited data states have Q*<=2. For physical minority mu(g)=min(P[g=-1],P[g=+1]), every node obeys Q*_v<=4mu(g_v)log2(1/mu(g_v)); at the root Q*=[D_selector-C 2^{-(r+k)}]_+<4*2^{-k}mu(F)log2(1/mu(F))<=mu(F)log2(1/mu(F))/4 and Q*<=2^{1-k}I(F). At r=2k and fixed finite C, Q*/I(F) is asymptotic to (2/5)2^{-k}. In particular the C=6 reserve certificate gives H(F)<=(6+2^{1-k})I(F)<=49I(F)/8. Pointwise credit domination is not a local drift assertion for the rarity function, which remains false on these selector roots for fixed coefficients.
